facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman was named in 2015 based on fossils found near Iquitos, Peru.
facts.quote: The species was named in 2015 on the basis of one nearly complete skull and a second partial skull from the Pebas Formation near Iquitos, Peru.

facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman had a short, rounded snout and blunt back-jaw teeth adapted for crushing freshwater bivalves.
facts.quote: K. iquitosensis is characterized by a short, rounded snout and blunt teeth at the back of its jaws that were likely adapted to crushing freshwater bivalves.

facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman grew to an estimated total length of 171.2 to 189.1 cm.
facts.quote: Its estimated total body length is 171.2 to 189.1 cm.

facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman lived in the Amazon basin approximately 13 million years ago during the Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: Kuttanacaiman lived in what is now the Amazon basin during the Middle Miocene, approximately 13 million years ago (Ma).

facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman lived in the Pebas Mega-Wetland System, a massive wetland covering over 1,000,000 km² before the Amazon River Basin formed.
facts.quote: Kuttanacaiman lived in Amazonia at a time before the Amazon River Basin was established; in its place was a massive wetland, called the Pebas Mega-Wetland System, that covered an approximate area of over 1000000 km2

facts.statement: Fossil beds of the bivalve genus Pachydon suggest it was a food source for Kuttanacaiman in swamps and marshes.
facts.quote: Shells belonging to the bivalve genus Pachydon form thick fossil beds in the Pebas Formation and may have been a food source for Kuttanacaiman and these other caimans in swamps and marshes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that crushing dentition was an ancestral trait for the Caimaninae clade because basal members like Gnatusuchus and Globidentosuchus also possessed it.
facts.quote: Other basal caimanines such as Gnatusuchus and Globidentosuchus also possess crushing teeth, suggesting that this type of dentition was ancestral for the clade.

facts.statement: The genus name comes from the Quechua word kuttana, meaning "grinding or crushing machine," while the species name honors the native peoples of Iquitos.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene de la palabra quechua kuttana, que significa "máquina trituradora", mientras que el nombre de la especie es en honor de los pueblos nativos de Iquitos.

facts.statement: Kuttanacaiman lived between 15.98 and 11.63 million years ago during the Langhian to Serravallian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Serravallian (15.98 to 11.63 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates Kuttanacaiman is one of the most basal members of the Caimaninae clade.
rejected.quote: A phylogenetic analysis published in 2015 indicates that Kuttanacaiman is one of the most basal members of the clade Caimaninae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Kuttanacaiman is one of the most basal members'
